note: The wire schema of a repo's `workflow.yml`, as data (#880 slice A).
This file is the shared statement of what a workflow file is, and two tests hold each
side to it. What they pin, exactly:
src-tauri/tests/orchestration.rs
- every section's FIELD NAMES against the engine's `Raw*` serde types, both
directions, with no exclusion list;
- each field's `values`, `default`, `min`, `max`, `maxLength` and `max_entries` against the
engine's own accessors and constants (SUPPORTED_CLIS, kind_names,
role_hint_names, intake_source_names, builtin_intake_profile, the
MergeQueuePolicy/ResourcePolicy Default impls, RESOURCE_*, NOTIFY_EXPIRES_*,
RESOURCES_MAX) — and in both directions, so metadata cannot be added here
that the engine never stated;
- `on_out_of_range` BEHAVIORALLY: the test drives `parse_workflow` with an
out-of-range value and checks whether it refuses the file or clamps the value.
test/workflowschema.test.ts
- the pane's parser reads every field (it never lands in the unknown-key bag);
- the pane's canonical serializer emits every field, so a save drops nothing;
- every enum value declared here is one the pane's own validator accepts, and a
value outside the set is refused;
- every field is either claimed by a form control or listed as not yet having one.
NOT pinned, so nobody assumes otherwise:
- `title` and `help` prose, and the `types` legend below;
- `gate.require`'s value set, which is hand-listed in workflow.rs because the
engine states it only as match arms — there is no accessor to ask;
- the pane has no validation rule of its own for `effort` or `context`, which are
capability data the backend answers per CLI and model (`agent_cli_knobs`), so the
TS enum check covers only the fields it does validate; full engine-parity for a
live buffer is `workflow_check`'s job. (`intake.source` LEFT this list in #1020,
when the pane gained the form that writes it: it now has `isIntakeSource` plus an
`intake-unknown-source` finding, and the enum check above feeds this manifest's
own `intake.source` values through it.)
It describes loomux's OWN product schema — the shape of a workflow file, never any
particular repo's roster (CLAUDE.md constraint 8). `blocks:` is data; what is pinned
here is what a block IS.
Adding a field: add it to the engine's `Raw*` struct, to this manifest, to the pane's
model (`src/workflowmodel.ts` — KNOWN_* + the emitters), and to a form descriptor. The
tests refuse to let you stop after the first step.

types.multiline: free text over many lines (emitted as a YAML block scalar)
types.number: an integer; `min`/`max` state the engine's own bounds where it has any
types.enum: one of `values` — a closed set this build refuses to go outside of
types.path: a repo-relative file path (never absolute, never escaping the repo)
types.block-ref: the `id` of a block declared in this same file
types.section: a nested mapping whose shape is the section named in `section`
types.section-map: a mapping of author-chosen names to `section` mappings

field_keys.name: the key as it is spelled in the file
field_keys.values: for `enum`: every value the ENGINE accepts, including the empty string where an empty value is meaningful (`block.cli`, `intake.source`) — a control that cannot represent one of these cannot represent a legal file
field_keys.default: what the engine BEHAVES as when the key is omitted (the placeholder a form shows), which is not always the wire default — `merge_queue.max_batch` is absent on the wire and 3 in effect
field_keys.maxLength: longest accepted STRING, in BYTES as the engine counts it (`check_segment` compares `s.len()`) — distinct from `max`, which bounds a number. A generated text control sets its maxlength from this, and an HTML maxlength counts UTF-16 code units: the two agree only while the field's alphabet is ASCII, which `block.remote`'s is and a future field's may not be. DECLARING THIS COMMITS THE ENGINE: the manifest pin panics on any field that declares a bound the engine states no fact for, so a limit documented here without a matching `workflow_schema_field_facts()` entry reddens CI rather than informing a control
field_keys.on_out_of_range: `refuse` = the engine rejects the whole file; `clamp` = it silently pulls the value into range. A generated control must refuse the submit in the first case and may accept-and-coerce in the second
field_keys.max_entries: for `section-map`: how many entries the engine will load before refusing the file
field_keys.required: the engine has no default for this — a file without it does not load
field_keys.section: for the container types: which section describes the value's shape
field_keys.help: prose for the human, rendered beside the control

workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.help: The top level of the file: what this workflow is called, and the sections it declares.

fields.name: version
fields.help: The schema version this file speaks. This build reads and writes version 1; anything else is refused rather than guessed at.

fields.name: name
fields.help: Display name for the workflow. Cosmetic — nothing references it.

fields.name: authored_with
fields.help: The loomux version that CREATED the file. Informational, never a validation error, and never restamped on save — it records who authored the workflow, not who last looked at it.

fields.name: blocks
fields.help: The agents a run may use. Order matters: the first block of a capability class is what an unrouted spawn of that class resolves to.

fields.name: edges
fields.help: The declared happy path. ADVISORY — the orchestrator still decides when to spawn what.

fields.name: gates
fields.help: What must be true before a merge. ENFORCED in the `gh` PATH shim, not in a prompt. Keyed by gate name; today the only gate is `merge`.

fields.name: intake
fields.help: Where autonomous work comes from, and what its label vocabulary is called. Absent = loomux's built-in profile.

fields.name: merge_queue
fields.help: Policy for the bisecting merge queue on orchestrator-owned integration branches. Absent = off, and behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

fields.name: driver
fields.help: Policy for the engine-driven review-loop driver (#1778). Absent = off, and behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. The counters are closed ranges held to the orchestrator template's INVARIANT 9 - a value outside the range refuses the whole file.

fields.name: resources
fields.help: Named lock resources agents may acquire, keyed by a name this repo chooses (loomux never learns what it means). Absent = the lock tools are not offered at all.

fields.name: board
fields.help: Task-board policy — how much work may sit in each status at once. Absent = no limits, and behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

block.title: Block
block.help: One agent: who it is, what capability class it runs as, and what it runs on.

fields.name: id
fields.help: Immutable identity — edges and gates name THIS, never the display name. Lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_'.

fields.name: name
fields.help: Display label. Renaming it can never break a reference; that is its whole point.

fields.name: kind
fields.help: The capability class. CLOSED: a workflow file may define any persona, but it can never invent a capability. `manager` is the human's own interface pane — at most one per workflow, never spawned by the orchestrator, and (like `orchestrator`) it may not declare prompt/profile/allow.

fields.name: cli
fields.help: The agent CLI this block spawns on. The empty value is a real one and the state most blocks are in: it inherits the group's CLI, which is picked at launch. A named CLI must also be able to host this block's kind — the engine refuses e.g. a reviewer on a CLI with no tool-level edit deny.

fields.name: model
fields.help: The model to pin for this block. Empty = the CLI's own default.

fields.name: prompt
fields.help: Inline persona, compiled to the CLI's native inline-agent flag. Mutually exclusive with `profile`.

fields.name: profile
fields.help: Persona FILE, repo-relative (e.g. .github/agents/worker.md). Mutually exclusive with `prompt`.

fields.name: allow
fields.help: Extra pre-approved tool patterns, e.g. "Bash(gh pr view --json title,body)". Refused on a read-only kind, and it can never re-grant a denied tool — deny beats allow on every CLI.

fields.name: role_hint
fields.help: A persona/template marker. It cannot change the block's capability CLASS — that is `kind` — but it can change which MCP tools the block is offered, from a list loomux enumerates. `advisor` requires kind: planner, `process` requires kind: worker, `liaison` requires kind: reviewer.

fields.name: effort
fields.help: Thinking level, from the CLI's own vocabulary. Which values exist (and whether the CLI has the seam at all) is the backend's answer — `agent_cli_knobs` — never a list mirrored here. Empty = the CLI's default.

fields.name: context
fields.help: Context-window variant, e.g. "1m". Same ownership as `effort`: the backend states what is deliverable. Empty = the model's own window.

fields.name: remote
fields.help: An abstract LABEL for a machine this block's agent runs on over SSH. The repo file only ever SELECTS a name; the OPERATOR binds it to a host, an account and a remote clone path outside the repo — so there is no host/port/identity_file key here, and writing one fails the whole file. Requires kind: worker, reviewer or planner and an explicitly spelled cli: claude. Letters, digits, '-' and '_', at most 64 characters, not starting with '-'. Absent = a local block, which is every block today: the key does nothing until the operator binds it.

edge.title: Connection
edge.help: One advisory hand-off. The file may write `to:` as a list to fan out; each target reads as one connection.

fields.name: from
fields.help: The block this hand-off leaves.

fields.name: to
fields.help: The block it points at. A list here (`to: [rev-a, rev-b]`) is a fan-out — one connection per target.

gate.title: Merge gate
gate.help: What must be recorded before loomux will let `gh pr merge` through.

fields.name: require
fields.help: `all-pass` = every named reviewer recorded PASS. `threshold` = at least N of them did. `all` is an accepted synonym for `all-pass`; `all-pass` is the spelling loomux writes. Omitting the key with a `threshold: N` present means a threshold gate.

fields.name: threshold
fields.help: How many passing reviews a `threshold` gate needs. Meaningless — and refused above the reviewer count — otherwise.

fields.name: reviewers
fields.help: The blocks whose verdict the gate waits for. Each must be a reviewer-kind block, or the gate could never open.

fields.name: also
fields.help: Extra conditions, e.g. "ci-green", "body-unchanged", "base-green". The backend owns what each one means, and a condition this build cannot check refuses the merge rather than being ignored.

fields.name: max_diff_lines
fields.help: The largest PR, in changed lines (additions + deletions), this gate will let through. Omit the key for no limit — 0 is refused, because a bound that bounds nothing is a typo. A PR whose size cannot be read is refused too.

fields.name: routing
fields.help: Path-based reviewer routing: rules that ADD required reviewers when the PR's changed files match one of their globs. The required set is `reviewers` plus every rule that matched, so a rule can only ever make this gate stricter. Absent = no routing, and no changed-file lookup at all. Cannot be combined with `require: threshold` — a threshold counts votes over a fixed list, and routing makes the list depend on the diff.

gate.routing.title: Routing rule
gate.routing.help: One path-routing rule: if this PR changed any file matching `paths`, these reviewers are required too. Globs use `*` only — any run of characters, INCLUDING `/` — a leading `**/` is optional, and the match is anchored at both ends. Deliberately coarse: over-matching asks for one more review, under-matching skips one the repo asked for, and only one of those is survivable. A PR whose changed-file list loomux cannot account for refuses the merge rather than being read as "no rule matched".

fields.name: paths
fields.help: Path globs, matched against the PR's changed files. Letters, digits, '.', '_', '-', '/' and '*'. Write file globs, not directories: `src/**`, never `src/`, `/src/**` or a `..` segment — those match nothing at all, so they are refused rather than silently never firing.

fields.name: reviewers
fields.help: Reviewer blocks required when any path matches. Validated exactly as the gate's own `reviewers:` are — the block must exist and be `kind: reviewer` — because a rule naming anything else could never be satisfied.

intake.title: Intake
intake.help: Where autonomous work comes from. Inert vocabulary plus an adapter chosen from a fixed set — there is deliberately no spelling here that can weaken the human merge gate.

fields.name: source
fields.help: Which adapter supplies work. `github-labels` polls issues by label (today's wired behavior); `board` and `none` are schema-reserved. The empty value is accepted and means the default, so a repo can override just the labels without restating a source it already means.

fields.name: labels
fields.help: This repo's label spellings. Declare one and the other four keep their built-in defaults.

intake.labels.title: Intake labels
intake.labels.help: The label vocabulary intake matches on. Letters, digits, '-' and '_', and it may not begin with '-' (a leading dash would be read as a flag where the label becomes a command argument) — a label that would need rewriting is refused, never silently changed.

fields.name: ready
fields.help: "Build this." — groomed, go.

fields.name: investigate
fields.help: "Look, don't build." — research only; findings go on the issue.

fields.name: owned
fields.help: "Mine." — an orchestrator has taken this issue.

fields.name: prototype
fields.help: "Build it for a demo." — feedback-gated work.

fields.name: hold
fields.help: "Held by the human — do not start this." The one veto in the vocabulary: under full autonomy every open issue is eligible except the ones carrying this label. Unlike the four fields above, renaming this one takes effect everywhere — the intake poller, the issues-view hold button, and the orchestrator's own contract all use the spelling you declare here.

merge_queue.title: Merge queue
merge_queue.help: Policy for the bisecting merge queue (#581). Policy, not mechanism: nothing here names a branch or a verification command — the queue observes the repo's own CI, and the target comes from the enqueued PR's live base.

fields.name: enabled
fields.help: Off by default. Off means every queue path is unreachable, not merely unused.

fields.name: max_batch
fields.help: How many approved sub-PRs one speculative batch may carry. At 3, a red batch costs at most 2 extra CI runs to attribute.

fields.name: checks_timeout_minutes
fields.help: Backstop on waiting for a batch's checks, so a repo with no checks attached surfaces as unverifiable instead of pending in silence. Clamped into range rather than refused.

driver.title: Review driver
driver.help: Policy for the engine-driven review-loop driver (#1778 §5.3). Policy, not mechanism: nothing here names a PR or starts a drive — no drive exists until an orchestrator makes its own role-gated drive_review call naming one PR. The counters are INVARIANT 9's numbers, and a repo may run a tighter loop than they promise but never a looser one.

fields.name: enabled
fields.help: Off by default. Off means every drive path is unreachable, not merely unused.

fields.name: max_review_rounds
fields.help: Review-finding rounds one drive may spend. INVARIANT 9 promises the orchestrator three; the driver may run tighter, never looser.

fields.name: max_ci_attempts
fields.help: CI attempts one drive may spend. Same invariant, same direction.

fields.name: max_rebase_attempts
fields.help: Rebase attempts one drive may spend. INVARIANT 9 grants one; 0 is legal (a repo may refuse the driver any rebase), 2 is refused.

fields.name: lane_timeout_minutes
fields.help: Backstop on a reviewer lane producing a verdict, so a stalled lane surfaces as held(lane-stalled) instead of pending in silence. Clamped into range rather than refused, like every notify-TTL wait.

fields.name: fix_timeout_minutes
fields.help: Backstop on a resumed worker pushing or reporting. Same clamp family.

fields.name: drive_timeout_minutes
fields.help: Last-resort backstop on the drive's whole age, under the four per-state bounds that do the work. Twelve hours, on its OWN range rather than the notify-TTL family the two waits above ride: a backstop measured in the same hours as those waits is the one clock a drive making steady progress can still trip. Time the live-delegate cap refused this drive a lane is excluded from it.

resource.title: Lock resource
resource.help: One named thing agents must take turns on. Restrict-only: the whole schema is two numbers, and the worst a declaration can do is make an agent wait.

fields.name: slots
fields.help: How many agents may hold it at once. 1 (the default) is a mutex; a repo that wants a semaphore says so.

fields.name: max_hold_minutes
fields.help: How long one hold may last before the sweep reclaims it — the bound that keeps a crashed holder from parking the resource forever.

board.title: Board
board.help: Task-board policy (#1175). Kanban WIP limits: `max live agents` caps concurrent agents, this caps concurrent WORK, so "finish before you start" is mechanical rather than prose.

fields.name: wip
fields.help: Per-status caps on how many work items may sit in a status at once. A status you omit has no cap.

fields.name: enforce
fields.help: false (the default) = a crossing warns the orchestrator and audits, and the write still lands. true = an AGENT's write crossing a cap is refused; the human's own board edits still only warn, under either setting.

board.wip.title: WIP limits
board.wip.help: One cap per board status, counted over LEAF work items (a container's status is a rollup of its children, so counting both would count the same work twice). `done` has no field on purpose: it is the relief valve every other cap depends on.

fields.name: queued
fields.help: Cap on the backlog — kanban's input queue limit. Omit for no cap.

fields.name: in-progress
fields.help: Cap on work being actively done. The usual first limit to set. Omit for no cap.

fields.name: review
fields.help: Cap on items with a reviewer engaged — half of the review-debt signal. Omit for no cap.

fields.name: pr
fields.help: Cap on open PRs past review, waiting on the human's merge gate — the other half of review debt. Omit for no cap.

fields.name: prototype
fields.help: Cap on demo-gated drafts awaiting the human's promote/scrap verdict. Omit for no cap.

fields.name: human-testing
fields.help: Cap on items parked for the human to validate. Omit for no cap.

fields.name: blocked
fields.help: Cap on blocked work. Prefer leaving this one uncapped under `enforce: true` — refusing a move to `blocked` refuses an agent's report of reality. Omit for no cap.
